absent: How per-address statuses are determined inside the batch scorer and what each status value means.
How pages are moved between nodes including ordering, retries, and per-page error reporting.
Permission model details for ptrace access checks and LSM move-memory hooks beyond their invocation.
Allocation, reclaim, compaction and huge-page support internals behind folio helpers and GFP modes.
Page-table, reverse-mapping, TLB, cache and MMU-notifier mechanics behind walk, lock, and migration-entry helpers.
Device unmap, copy and finalize steps that consume collected arrays, including failure recovery.
Swap cache, swap device lifetime, and shared-memory error-entry handling beyond the observed branches.
Hugetlb locking, huge-state lookup, and marker-entry lifecycle beyond the residency sampling shown.
Exact numeric values and bit layouts for migration flags, selection flags, protection bits and error codes.
Concurrency rules for VMA lifetime, address-space teardown, and driver owner matching beyond the fragments.

findings.text: Move pages system entry accepts a target process identifier plus page count plus user arrays for addresses and nodes and statuses plus option flags and forwards all of them unchanged to the internal move or query handler.

Device migration setup validates caller supplied range and arrays and fault page, clears caller source area, resets counters, walks the range to collect candidates, unmaps when candidates exist, and reports success so the driver may copy stable contents.
Device migration copy stage forwards collected source entries plus destination entries plus total count plus private context to the shared device page mover.
Device migration finalize stage forwards collected source entries plus destination entries plus total count plus optional fault page to the shared device finalizer.

Contiguous physical range helper locks each folio starting from a base frame number, marks compound heads, truncates with zeroes when a folio would extend past the requested length, then unmaps the whole array without a fault page.
Scatter frame helper locks each folio named by an input frame array, marks compound heads in place, truncates with zeroes on length overrun, then unmaps the whole array without a fault page.
Move handler only permits the flag MPOL_MF_MOVE and the flag MPOL_MF_MOVE_ALL, rejecting other bits as invalid, and demands the capability CAP_SYS_NICE when the second flag is requested.

Target lookup with zero identifier returns current address space with extra reference and current node mask, otherwise it finds task by numeric identifier, takes exec update lock interruptibly, validates ptrace access, validates LSM move permission, records node mask, grabs task address space, releases lock and task reference, and normalizes absent task or empty result to distinct errors.

Status query walks the requested pages in fixed-size batches, fetching each batch of user pointers through a compat or native path, scoring the batch against the target address space, storing back per-page status, advancing offset and remaining count, aborting on any user copy fault and reporting fault unless fully consumed.
Status query batch capacity is sixteen entries, applied to both temporary pointer and status arrays and to the per-iteration limit.

Misplaced destination allocator pins allocation to the supplied node, uses a light transparent huge page mode for compound orders and a movable high-user mode without reclaim plus no-retry and no-warn and no-memalloc for order zero, then allocates the same order on that node.

Setup rejects missing source or destination arrays, missing VMA, huge-TLB or special or DAX VMAs, non-positive page counts, and any start or end outside the VMA bounds, and requires an optional fault page to be device-private and already locked.
Collection brackets the page table walk with migrate-type MMU notifier invalidate start and end carrying the driver owner, then shrinks the recorded end to cover exactly the number of slots visited.

Migration context carries a VMA pointer plus byte range plus source and destination arrays plus total and candidate counters plus selection flags plus device owner plus fault page, with source encoding per-page state and destination initially cleared.

Each visited page produces one slot pair where zero in both arrays means skip, migrate mark means candidate for moving, plus optional write mark preserving writability and optional compound mark for huge heads with following slots zeroed for tail coverage.

Huge PMD path distinguishes empty entries routed to hole handling, transparent huge entries requiring system selection and non-zero backing, device-private entries requiring matching selection and owner, and ordinary tables that retry at PTE level, with compound-alignment allowing a single PMD migration entry otherwise falling back to split and PTE walk.

PTE walk treats empty entries as migratable only for anonymous VMAs, ignores non-device swap entries, filters normal and coherent device pages by selection and owner, splits large folios and restarts the range, pins and try-locks each candidate, replaces its entry with a migration swap entry preserving dirty and young and soft-dirty and userfault bits, and flushes TLB only when at least one present mapping was removed.

Task lookup holds the target signal exec update lock for read in interruptible mode across credential and security checks and address space acquisition, releasing it before dropping the task reference.

Device collection serializes huge entries with the PMD lock and small entries with the PTE map lock under lazy MMU mode, references each folio to pin it, uses non-blocking folio lock except for the fault folio that is already held, and keeps the reference until after rmap removal or failure cleanup.

Folio split helper takes the folio lock only when the folio differs from the fault folio, consumes the extra reference it was given on large device or normal pages, and on success transfers lock and reference ownership to the post-split folio containing the fault page.
Huge-TLB residency check holds the huge PTE lock while sampling the entry and filling per-page residency bytes, then releases before returning.
Huge-TLB residency reports each subpage as resident unless the huge entry is empty or a marker, writing one byte per page and advancing the caller cursor.

Swap residency treats non-swap entries as present for non-shared anonymous cases and absent for shared memory error cases, requires swap support, looks up shared swap devices safely, and otherwise reports up-to-date status of any cached folio.

Move and stat paths fail cleanly on user copy faults, disallowed flags, missing privilege, unknown task, interrupted lock wait, denied ptrace or LSM checks, and empty address spaces, returning distinct negative errors without partial state.

Collection is best-effort under contention where folio lock failure, failed split, zero backing, unowned device memory, unmapped or uncached pages, and length overruns all degrade to zeroed skip entries rather than blocking or reporting errors, with TLB flush deferred and conditional.
Device walk binds the custom PMD entry handler and hole handler with read walk locking, so huge and missing ranges are intercepted while mapped PTEs flow through the detailed collector.

After collection the setup path invokes the device unmap over all collected source slots when at least one candidate exists, replacing the candidate count with the unmapped count before returning control to the driver.
Collection advances one page per slot and derives total bytes from slot count shifted by page order, while huge compound handling requires both range ends aligned to PMD huge size.
Single frame locker resolves the struct page for a frame, ignores tail pages, pins the folio, attempts non-blocking lock, and encodes success as a migratable frame value or zero on any miss.
Driver flow is setup to collect and unmap and stabilize contents, then driver copy into allocated memory, then copy stage to install pages, then finalize to restore or complete entries.
